html:
Cambodia is the country of the Khmer people on the lower Mekong river and the great lake Tonlé Sap. It is the heir of the Khmer Empire of Angkor. The map shows it from 1492 to 1815 and again from 1938 to 2010.

After Ayutthaya sacked Angkor in 1431, the court moved south toward Phnom Penh, where river trade was easier. Cambodia then spent four centuries squeezed between two stronger neighbours:

  • Siam (Sukhothai and Ayutthaya), which took the royal city of Longvek in 1594;
  • Vietnam, whose settlers moved into the Mekong delta in the 1600s and 1700s, turning the Khmer port of Prey Nokor into Saigon (Cochinchina).

In 1863 King Norodom accepted French protection to escape both, and Cambodia became part of French Indochina. French scholars studied and restored Angkor.

Cambodia became independent in 1953 under Norodom Sihanouk. It was dragged into the Vietnam War and heavily bombed by the United States. In April 1975 the communist Khmer Rouge took Phnom Penh and at once emptied the cities. Under Pol Pot some 1.5 to 2 million people died of execution, hunger and forced labour, the Cambodian genocide. Vietnam invaded in 1979 and drove them out. After a United Nations run election in 1993 the monarchy came back, with Sihanouk as king again.
sum: Cambodia is the country of the Khmer people on the lower Mekong river and the great lake Tonlé Sap. It is the heir of the Khmer Empire of Angkor. The map shows it from 1492 to 1815 and again from 1938 to 2010.
